identity.plain_name: A hinge that clicks and stays put at one or more set angles, such as a cabinet door that clicks open at 90° or a sofa headrest that clicks up a notch at a time
aliases: position hinge / positioning hinge (Southco's category name, which also covers friction hinges)
ratchet hinge / ratchet fitting (furniture: sofa headrests, armrests, backrests)
adjustable hinge fitting (reclining chairs and folding stands; patent US3232136)
bistable hinge (a detent variant with a spring that drives the door to its open or closed position; Southco)
locking hinge (maker name, often for a hinge that locks at one angle)
click hinge or locking hinge plate (LEGO (brand) hinge plates that click through set positions)
identity.one_liner: A hinge with a built-in click mechanism (a spring pressing a ball, wedge, tooth or springy arm into notches, or a pawl in a toothed segment) that holds a lid, door, leg or backrest at preset angles until it is pushed firmly on.
identity.complexity: A small assembly that acts as one unit: two hinge leaves joined by a pin or knuckle, plus a detent inside the knuckle. Common detents: a spring pushing a ball, roller, wedge or toothed part into notches (Elesa: 'an applied force from the internal spring'); a steel detent tube (Southco C6); spring wires pushing toothed floating wedges against gear teeth (patent EP2389839); or a pawl and toothed segment (furniture ratchet fittings). Printed versions: two leaves plus a flexible (TPU) toothed ring or a springy printed arm (Printables 'Clicking Hinge').
identity.how_it_works: Two main kinds exist. In a click-stop detent hinge, a spring presses something (a ball, roller, wedge, toothed ring or springy arm) against notches that turn with the other leaf; at each preset angle it drops into a notch and holds the door there, and pushing the door firmly bends or compresses the spring so it rides out and on to the next notch, in either direction (Southco: 'opens and locks into place at a pre-set angle, usually with a distinctive click'; Elesa). In a ratchet-fitting hinge (sofas, headrests, reclining chairs), a pawl clicks over teeth as you raise the part so it holds at each step and can't fold back down; to lower it you move it all the way past the last step, where a projection knocks the pawl out of the teeth and a spring holds it clear, so the part can swing freely back to its starting position (Lear headrest patent US5236245A; US3232136 describes a similar release at the end of travel). A bistable variant uses a spring that pushes the door to one of two end positions (Southco).

job: let it move (turn, slide or bend): it is still a hinge that swings
click into set positions: holds the lid, door or backrest at preset angles
stop it moving back (one-way): ratchet-fitting types hold against folding back down until they are reset at the end of travel
finder_attributes.motion: rotate, usually within about 180° (e.g. Southco C6/G6 detent hinges: 180° range of motion with detents at 80°, 115°, 150° or 120° and 170°; Elesa: detents at -90°, 0°, +70° and +115°)
special_behaviour: indexing (clicks into set positions): holds at preset angles with a click you can feel
one-way (moves freely one way, locks the other): ratchet-fitting hinges click up but won't fold down until reset (US5236245A)
over-centre (snaps past a point and stays): bistable hinges drive the door to a preset open or closed position by themselves (Southco)
holding_principle: spring force (a spring or springy part presses it in place): click-stop types; the holding torque is set by the spring and notch shape
shape (the parts interlock; form-fit): ratchet-fitting types, where the pawl's locking face sits against a tooth
finder_attributes.removability: removable: screwed, bolted or riveted to the two parts like an ordinary hinge (rivets make it semi-permanent)
finder_attributes.reuse_cycles: many times: can be unscrewed and refitted; commercial detent hinges are tested for tens of thousands of open-close cycles, e.g. more than 20,000 (Elesa) and up to 20,000 (Southco C6/G6)
finder_attributes.tools_needed: screwdriver or hex key (or a rivet tool); none to operate
finder_attributes.load: light to medium: the hinge pin carries the door's weight well, but the detent only resists a small turning force; e.g. 0.70 Nm forward and reverse detent torque for a Southco C6-227 and around 3 Nm for Elesa detent hinges. Furniture ratchet fittings are built to hold a person leaning on a backrest (US3232136, US5236245A) [uncertain] (no load figures found).
finder_attributes.adjustable: Only between the built-in positions: the detent angles are fixed by the design (e.g. 80°, 115°, 150° or 120° and 170° in Southco's C6 range). Holding strength is chosen when buying (Southco offers three positioning torque ratings in the C6 series; printed designs can swap a softer or harder detent ring, Printables 'Clicking Hinge').
finder_attributes.play_and_precision: small to noticeable: returns to the same angle every time, but a spring detent has some give either side of each position, and ratchet fittings can move back a little before the pawl catches a tooth [uncertain]. Needs the two leaves mounted in line; a bent or misaligned mounting makes the detent stiff or uneven [uncertain].
finder_attributes.access_needed: one side only (blind) when the leaves are screwed into thick parts; both sides when bolts and nuts go through thin panels
finder_attributes.materials: Technopolymer (glass-filled nylon), zinc die-cast and stainless steel (Elesa); acetal copolymer leaves with a stainless steel detent tube, polyamide and zinc alloy (Southco); zinc-plated steel for furniture ratchet hinges (redesignstore). Printed versions: PLA or PETG leaves with a TPU (flexible) detent gear (Printables 'Clicking Hinge').
finder_attributes.maker_difficulty: easy to moderate: easy to buy and screw on, or to print a small clicking hinge with a flexible insert; moderate to make one that holds a heavy lid firmly for many cycles

processes: off-the-shelf part: detent hinges, positioning hinges and ratchet fittings in plastic, zinc and steel
3D print (FDM): small clicking hinges for boxes, stands and enclosures, often with a TPU detent insert
woodwork: fitting bought detent or ratchet hinges to cabinets, lids and furniture
sheet metal: stamped steel ratchet fittings for furniture
injection moulding: plastic detent hinges and toy click hinges (e.g. LEGO (brand)) [uncertain]
making.print_in_place: partly: several printed designs need assembly, e.g. BaGooN's 'Clicking Hinge' (Printables) has a separately printed flexible TPU inner gear that is snapped into a two-part case; some print-in-place hinges lock at a single angle by sliding along their axis (chandler's 'Locking Hinge 90' and 'Locking Hinge 180', Printables), which is a lock rather than a multi-click detent.
making.making_tips_3d_printing: 1) Easiest printable detent: make the detent part flexible. BaGooN's clicking hinge prints its toothed inner gear in TPU and the leaves in PLA or PETG at 0.3 mm layers, 2 perimeters and 15% infill with no supports, and offers a harder gear for stronger holding (Printables 'Clicking Hinge'). 2) Or use a springy printed arm pressing on a notched ring inside the knuckle (a compliant detent); lay the arm flat on the bed, fillet its root to at least half its thickness and avoid building it vertically in Z (Protolabs/Hubs snap-fit guide). 3) Make the arm or spring sit relaxed (unbent) at each detent position, because plastic springs held bent creep and relax (DuPont design guide, pp. 36 and 47) and PLA creeps most (thrinter test); otherwise the hinge will slowly lose its hold. 4) Work out the turning load the detent must resist: the lid's weight times the sideways distance from the hinge pin to its centre of gravity; a light but long lid can need as much holding as a heavy short one (Southco). Printed detents hold only small torques, so add a stay or use two hinges for heavier lids [uncertain]. 5) Print the leaves flat with the knuckle axis horizontal so the knuckle's layers aren't split by bending loads (layer adhesion is roughly half the in-plane strength; CNC Kitchen) [uncertain] (orientation depends on design). 6) For print-in-place pins, keep at least about 0.3 mm clearance (Prusa) to 0.5 mm (Protolabs/Hubs FDM) between moving surfaces; the first movements may be stiff and loosen with use (chandler, Printables 'Locking Hinge 90'). 7) PETG is a good all-round choice for leaves (used by several of these designs); PLA softens from about 60 °C (CNC Kitchen), so avoid it for hinges in cars or sunny windows.
making.off_the_shelf_parts: Search for: 'detent hinge', 'positioning hinge', 'hinge with detent', 'hinge with indexing function', 'bistable hinge', 'ratchet hinge' or 'ratchet fitting' (sofa or headrest hinge, lift-up support), 'adjustable angle hinge', 'friction hinge' or 'torque hinge' (holds at any angle instead), 'lid stay'. Makers: Southco C6/G6 series (brand), Elesa CFA-F and Elesa+Ganter detent hinges (brand); CAD models of detent plastic hinges on TraceParts (via Printables).
rules_of_thumb: Choose a detent hinge for preset angles with a click, a constant-torque (friction) hinge for any angle, and a free-swinging hinge only for panels light enough to fall open under gravity (Southco 'How to Improve Function with Torque Hinges').
Detent hinges are usually set at 90° for cabinet doors and access panels (Southco).
Typical commercial holding torque per hinge: about 0.70 Nm (Southco C6-227) to about 3 Nm (Elesa); tested for more than 20,000 cycles (Elesa) or up to 20,000 (Southco C6/G6).

The load the detent must hold depends on the lid's weight and how far its centre of gravity is from the hinge axis: a light lid with a far centre of gravity can feel like a heavier lid with a near one (Southco 'How to Select the Right Level of Torque').
Southco C6/G6 detent hinges are rated from -40 °C to 80 °C (Southco product page).
Plastic springs used continuously under load creep and relax; springs under constant load should be steel (DuPont, p. 36).

everyday_examples: Sofa headrests, armrests and footrests that click through several angles (angle-adjustable sofa hinge, patent EP2389839), and seat headrests that click forward in steps and release when tilted fully forward (Lear patent US5236245A)
Reclining chairs and folding stands with a backrest that clicks to set angles (US3232136)
Cabinet doors, machine covers and access panels that click open and stay at 90° (Southco; Elesa)
LEGO (brand) click hinge plates, which step through set positions (e.g. a '1 x 2 Locking 9-Position' hinge plate, as named on Printables) [uncertain]
Adjustable laptop stands and folding table legs that click at several angles [uncertain] (not checked on an opened page)
guidance.when_to_use: Use a detent hinge when a lid, door, flap, leg or backrest should stop and stay at one or a few known angles without a separate stay or catch, and when a click that tells the user 'this is the right position' is helpful: equipment covers opened for service, display stands, folding supports, adjustable headrests and backrests. It is quicker than tightening a knob and more repeatable than a friction hinge. For 3D-printed boxes and stands, a detent hinge with a flexible insert or springy arm adds positions without metal parts.
guidance.when_not_to_use: Avoid it when the user needs any angle in between (use a friction or torque hinge), when the lid is heavy or long, because the detent may be overcome and the lid drop (use a counterbalance hinge, gas strut or lid stay), when the position must be locked against being knocked (use an indexing plunger through the hinge or a locking brace), or when you need fine, play-free angle steps under load (use a Hirth joint clamped by a bolt). For a single end position that must hold firmly, a latch or over-centre lock is better.
guidance.environment_limits: Southco's C6/G6 detent hinges are rated for -40 °C to 80 °C. Printed PLA leaves soften from about 60 °C (CNC Kitchen), and plastic springs or detent arms kept under load creep and lose their hold (DuPont; thrinter). Stainless steel and technopolymer versions suit wet, food and pharmaceutical settings (Elesa). Dirt and wear in the teeth or notches weaken the click over time [uncertain]; manufacturers suggest light lubrication for steel ratchet hinges (redesignstore).
guidance.safety_notes: Hinges are pinch points, especially ratchet fittings with teeth and moving pawls. A detent only holds a small turning force, so a lid or panel propped by a detent can fall if bumped or overloaded; keep heads and fingers clear of heavy lids and add a stay [uncertain]. On reclining furniture the reset action matters: early backrests could collapse under a seated person, which the ratchet fitting in US3232136 was designed to prevent. Moving a ratchet-fitted headrest to the end of its travel releases the pawl, so it will then swing freely back (US5236245A).
guidance.common_failures: The detent wears or the spring weakens, so the click becomes mushy and the lid drifts down [uncertain]; a printed detent arm or plastic spring creeps if held bent (DuPont). The lid is too heavy or too long for the hinge's holding torque, so it won't stay open (Southco's centre-of-gravity point). The flexible TPU insert wears or is too soft, fixed by printing a harder version (Printables 'Clicking Hinge'). A ratchet fitting doesn't reset, or releases unexpectedly at the top of its travel (US5236245A). Printed knuckles crack along layer lines [uncertain]. Avoid these by checking the torque needed, using two hinges or a stay for big lids, letting springs rest unloaded in each position, and choosing tough materials.
related: Friction hinge (torque hinge): holds at any angle by friction, with no clicks
Ratchet and pawl: the one-way toothed mechanism inside ratchet-fitting hinges
Compliant detent: a springy arm clicking into notches, which can be built into a printed hinge
Ball detent (spring plunger): a spring-loaded ball in dimples, a common detent inside hinges and levers
Indexing plunger: a pull-knob pin through holes in the hinge knuckle locks positions far more firmly
Hirth joint: toothed faces clamped by a bolt, for many fine, firmly locked angles
Bistable compliant mechanism: a one-piece flexure that snaps to one of two stable positions
Print-in-place hinge: a plain printed hinge with no holding positions
Folding-blade lock (slip joint): a spring bar gives a pocket-knife blade detent positions at open and closed
Clevis joint with thumbscrew: holds any angle by clamping, as on action-camera mounts
